cards.text: Rough week, friend. The Israelites just heard that everyone twenty and older who grumbled will fall in the wilderness, and their children will be the ones to enter the land, along with Caleb and Joshua (Numbers 14:29-31). Now the LORD speaks to Moses again, with a message for the Israelites.

cards.question: The LORD's new message for the Israelites starts by saying when these instructions kick in. When is it?

answers.text: After they enter the land He's giving them
While they wander in the wilderness
Once the forty years are halfway done

cards.text: He didn't say IF they enter, friend. He said AFTER, and then He starts talking about offerings from the herd or flock, for a vow, a freewill offering or an appointed feast, with a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

cards.question: When someone brings an animal from the herd or flock as an offering to the LORD, it doesn't come alone. What comes with it?

answers.text: A grain offering of fine flour and olive oil
A basket of the first ripe figs from the tree
A pair of young turtledoves from the flock

cards.question: True or false: With each lamb, the Israelites also prepare wine as a drink offering.

cards.text: Then God gets specific: a ram gets more flour, oil and wine than a lamb, a young bull gets more than that, and every bull, ram, lamb or goat gets its portion, no matter how many. Bigger animal, bigger batch. Friend, that's a RECIPE CARD, and I would frame it.
Every native-born Israelite does it this way. And for the generations to come, a foreigner living among them might want to bring a pleasing aroma to the LORD too.

cards.question: If a foreigner living among the Israelites wants to bring a food offering to the LORD, how does he do it?

answers.text: With half the flour and oil

cards.question: The LORD says the native-born and the foreigner will have the ___ law, and it's a ___ statute for the generations to come.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses another message for the Israelites. When they enter the land and eat its food, they're to lift up an offering to the LORD, and baker, I need you to sit down for this one.

cards.question: When the Israelites eat the food of the land, the LORD wants an offering from the first of something. What is it?

answers.text: The first of their olive oil

cards.text: DOUGH. God put DOUGH in the Law, and I have never felt so SEEN in my whole stamping life. They lift up a cake from the first of it as a contribution, just like an offering from the threshing floor.

cards.question: True or false: The offering from the first of the dough is a one-time gift for their first harvest in the land.

cards.text: Moses is still passing along the LORD's instructions for life in the land. Now the LORD turns to something else. What if they stray unintentionally and don't obey all the commands He's given through Moses, from the first day on down the generations?
You know, like setting the oven timer and never hitting start. And say the whole congregation slips up like that, without even knowing it.

cards.question: When the whole congregation sins unintentionally, what do they bring to the LORD?

answers.text: One young bull and one male goat
Two lambs and a pair of doves

cards.question: The priest makes atonement for the whole congregation, and because the sin was unintentional, they will be ___.
True or false: The foreigners living among the Israelites are forgiven right along with them.

cards.text: Now say just one person sins unintentionally. Friend, I know that one: I live alone in my bakery, so every upside-down cookie is a mystery with ONE suspect.

cards.question: When one person sins unintentionally, what does he bring as a sin offering?

answers.text: A young bull from the herd

cards.text: The priest makes atonement before the LORD for that person, and once it's done, he's forgiven. One mistake, one goat, one clean slate.

cards.question: True or false: For one person's unintentional sin, a foreigner living among the Israelites follows a different law than a native-born Israelite.

cards.text: But now the LORD draws a line. This isn't about straying by accident, it's about the person who sins defiantly, whether he's a native or a foreigner.

cards.question: The LORD says the person who sins defiantly is doing something against Him. What is it?
True or false: The person who sins defiantly can bring a sin offering and be forgiven, just like the one who sinned unintentionally.
The LORD says the person who sins defiantly will certainly be cut off from his people. Why?

answers.text: He despised the word of the LORD

findings.problem: "Rough week" and "The Israelites just heard" add a time span. Numbers 15:1 only says "Then," and Numbers 14 never says the events took a week or that chapter 15 follows right after.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card says the LORD speaks "with a message for the Israelites," which comes from Numbers 15:2 ("Speak to the Israelites and tell them"). The card cites only Numbers 15:1.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Numbers 15:3-12 is a stretch of offering rules with measurements. Card 6 sums most of it up, but card 5 asks about one of its measurement details: the wine for each lamb in verse 5.

rule.text: A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Then God gets specific...", "Bigger animal, bigger batch." and "Friend, that's a RECIPE CARD...". It is not the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "DOUGH.", "God put DOUGH in the Law..." and "They lift up a cake...".

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. It is the first card of stop 2, but it is not the passage's opening card, so the 3-sentence allowance doesn't apply.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 10 already says the defiant sinner can be "a native or a foreigner." That rules out the wrong answer "He wasn't born an Israelite" before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
